chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Allah, the Mighty and High, has not been revered with anything like the Appearance (al-Bada').

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu 'Abdillah, a common title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS).
key_terms.الْبَدَاءِ: The Appearance or Manifestation of God, referring to the change in divine decree or the revelation of previously hidden knowledge.
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and High, an honorific title for Allah.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of al-Bada' in Shia theology according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes *al-Bada’* not merely as a change in decree, but as the paramount attribute through which Allah’s majesty is magnified, distinguishing Him from static determinism. This concept, central to Shia theology, explains how divine knowledge interacts with time and circumstances, allowing for the alteration of fate through supplication or natural causes, thereby demonstrating God’s active sovereignty over creation.
